verses.zh: 亚玛谢登基的时候年二十五岁，在耶路撒冷作王二十九年。他母亲名叫约耶但，是耶路撒冷人。
verses.en: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1] His mother[NOTE:2] was Jehoaddan, who was from Jerusalem.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “the name of his mother.”
verses.commentary:
25:1 "Amaziah" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF THE DIVIDED KINGDOM.

2 Chronicles 25:1 is a typical introduction to a king's reign.

- age at ascension

- length of reign

- mother's name

"twenty-five years old. . .reigned twenty-nine years" For a good brief discussion, see Martin Selman,
Tyndale OT Commentaries, 2 Chronicles, p. 489.

"The date of Amaziah's reign is a seemingly intractable problem, and his twenty-nine years (v. 1)
has been reduced to varying lengths such as thirteen, sixteen, or nineteen years.1 One solution regards Amaziah as
sole ruler for only five years before being taken hostage by Jehoash of Israel (vv. 23-24), with his son Uzziah being
co-regent for the remaining twenty-four years. This rather surprising conclusion has found support in the unique
comment that Amaziah lived for fifteen years after Jehoash's death (v. 25) and in the participation of the people at
Uzziah's accession, perhaps indicating some kind of crisis (26:1; cf. 22:1).2 If this is correct, the two wars belong to
Amaziah's first five years, though the whole reign has been dated between 801-773 (Begrich) and796-767 (Thiele)."

The IVP Bible Background Commentary p. 446, mentions that Amaziah was a contemporary

- in Israel, of

- Joash

- Jeroboam II

- in Assyria, of

- Adad-Nirari III

- Shalmaneser IV

- Ashur-Dan III

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF ASSYRIA

verses.zh: 亚玛谢行耶和华眼中看为正的事，只是心不专诚。
verses.en: He did what the Lord approved,[NOTE:1] but not with wholehearted devotion.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he did what was proper in the eyes of the Lord.”
Heb “a complete heart.”
verses.commentary:
25:2 This is "good news; bad news." Amaziah did right in the sight of the Lord. See full note at 2 Chr. 24:2.
However, like his predecessors, he started well (i.e., listened to God's messengers, cf. vv. 5-10) but later did not (i.e.,
vv. 14-16,20; 2 Kgs. 14:4 mentions the high places).

David, the ideal king, had a "whole heart" but not all his descendants did.

- Solomon ‒ 1 Kgs. 11:4

- Abijam ‒ 1 Kgs. 15:3

David admonishes Solomon about this in 1 Chr. 28:8-9 and prays for him in 1 Chr. 29:19. Attitude is crucial!

verses.zh: 国一坚定，就把杀他父王的臣仆杀了，
verses.en: When he had secured control of the kingdom,[NOTE:1] he executed the servants who had assassinated his father the king.
notes: Heb “when the kingdom was secure upon him.”

verses.zh: 却没有治死他们的儿子，是照摩西律法书上耶和华所吩咐的说：「不可因子杀父，也不可因父杀子，各人要为本身的罪而死。」
verses.en: However, he did not execute their sons. He obeyed the Lord’s commandment as recorded in the law scroll of Moses,[NOTE:1] “Fathers must not be executed for what their sons do,[NOTE:2] and sons must not be executed for what their fathers do.[NOTE:3] A man must be executed only for his own sin.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “as it is written in the scroll of the law of Moses which the Lord commanded, saying.”
Heb “on account of sons.”
Heb “on account of fathers.”
This law is recorded in Deut 24:16.
verses.commentary:
25:4 This shows a knowledge of Deuteronomy (i.e., Deut. 24:16) before Josiah found the book of the law in the
house of the Lord. The Chronicler's writing shows he knew many OT books (see Introduction to 2 Chronicles, III., G.).

The parallel shows this same allusion (cf. 2 Kgs. 14:6) and, like the Chronicler, simply quoted him. Kings is
written earlier but still after the

- conquest of Jerusalem and the temple by Nebuchadnezzar

- the murder of Gedaliah the Babylonian appointed governor of Judah

Just a theological note, this verse focuses on the spiritual responsibility of each individual (cf. Jer. 31:29,30;
Ezekiel 18), but later in this chapter, several cities of Judah and 3,000 people are killed (2 Chr. 25:13) because of the sin of
Amaziah. It is hard to balance these concepts (i.e., Deut. 5:9 vs. 7:9)!

verses.zh: 亚玛谢招聚犹大人，按着犹大和便雅悯的宗族设立千夫长、百夫长，又数点人数，从二十岁以外，能拿枪拿盾牌出去打仗的精兵共有三十万；
verses.en: Amaziah assembled the people of Judah[NOTE:1] and assigned them by families to the commanders of units of 1,000 and the commanders of units of 100 for all Judah and Benjamin. He counted those twenty years old and up and discovered there were 300,000 young men of fighting age[NOTE:2] equipped with spears and shields.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Judah.” The words “the people of” are supplied in the translation for clarity. The Hebrew text uses the name “Judah” by metonymy here for the people of Judah.
Heb “young men going out to war.”
Heb “holding a spear and a shield.”
verses.commentary:
25:5 This is a census for military purposes of war (i.e., 2 Chr. 14:8; 17:14-18; 26:11-13) against Edom.

Josephus, Antiq. 9.1.1., says the battle was against three nations, "Amalekites, Edomites, and
Gebalites." The inclusion of "Amalekites" might be a way to explain/excuse the slaughter of 2 Chr. 25:12. All Amalekites
were to be killed.

SPECIAL TOPIC: EDOM AND ISRAEL

"300,000" As always in Kings and Chronicles, one wonders about the meaning of "thousand."

SPECIAL TOPIC: THOUSAND (eleph)

"spear and shield" It was the king's responsibility to produce, store, and distribute arms in this period. Often lists of
weaponry are mentioned.

- 2 Chr. 25:5; 11:12

- shields (i.e., large shield, BDB 857 III, KB 1037)

- spears or lance (BDB 942)

- 2 Chr. 14:8

- large shields (BDB 857 III)

- spears or lances (BDB 942)

- shields (BDB 171)

- bows (BDB 905)

- 2 Chr. 23:5

- spears (BDB 333)

- large shields (BDB 171)

- bows (BDB 1020, KB 1522)

- 2 Chr. 26:14

- shields (BDB 171, KB 545)

- spears (BDB 942)

- helmets (BDB 464)

- body armor (BDB 1056)

- bows (BDB 905)

- sling stones (BDB 6 construct BDB 887)

- Neh. 4:13

- swords (BDB 352)

- spears (BDB 942)

- bows (BDB 905)

See Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, "Armaments," pp. 241-246.

verses.zh: 又用银子一百他连得，从以色列招募了十万大能的勇士。
verses.en: He hired 100,000 Israelite warriors for 100 talents[NOTE:1] of silver.
notes: The Hebrew word כִּכַּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or, by extension, to a standard unit of weight. According to the older (Babylonian) standard the “talent” weighed 130 lbs. (58.9 kg), but later this was lowered to 108.3 lbs. (49.1 kg). More recent research suggests the “light” standard talent was 67.3 lbs. (30.6 kg). Using this as the standard for calculation, the weight of the silver was 6,730 lbs. (3,060 kg).
verses.commentary:
25:6 Amaziah hired mercenaries from Ephraim (2 Chr. 25:10).

"talents of silver" Apparently (i.e., from their actions in 2 Chr. 25:13) these Ephraimitic mercenaries were promised
part of the spoils of the defeated army.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE WEIGHTS AND VOLUMES

verses.zh: 有一个神人来见亚玛谢，对他说：「王啊，不要使以色列的军兵与你同去，因为耶和华不与以色列人以法莲的后裔同在。
verses.en: But a prophet[NOTE:1] visited him and said: “O king, the Israelite troops must not go with you, for the Lord is not with Israel or any of the Ephraimites.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “man of God.”
Heb “Israel, all the sons of Ephraim.”
verses.commentary:
25:7 Amaziah is confronted with a prophetic message which he obeyed (2 Chr. 25:7-10). This obedience brings
victory. The king's idolatry will bring defeat. Both are from YHWH, not human forces!

The post-exilic Chronicler (probably Ezra) is nervous of all foreign alliances. He chooses aspects of history
to emphasize his theological concern.

verses.zh: 你若一定要去，就奋勇争战吧！但　神必使你败在敌人面前；因为　神能助人得胜，也能使人倾败。」
verses.en: Even if you go and fight bravely in battle, God will defeat you[NOTE:1] before the enemy. God is capable of helping or defeating.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “cause you to stumble.”
Heb “to cause to stumble.”
verses.commentary:
25:8 There is an introductory series of three Qal�IMPERATIVES.

- if you go ‒ BDB 97, KB 112

- act ‒ BDB 793, KB 889

- be strong ‒ BDB 304, KB 302

This is a warning (v. 8, "do not let the army of Israel go with you," IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE
sense, same as #1). It is also a promise of YHWH's presence, power, and assured victory (cf. 2 Chr. 14:11; 20:6) if they are obedient.

verses.zh: 亚玛谢问神人说：「我给了以色列军的那一百他连得银子怎么样呢？」神人回答说：「耶和华能把更多的赐给你。」
verses.en: Amaziah asked the prophet:[NOTE:1] “But what should I do about the 100 talents of silver I paid the Israelite troops?” The prophet[NOTE:2] replied, “The Lord is capable of giving you more than that.”
notes: Heb “said to the man of God.”
Heb “man of God.”

verses.zh: 于是亚玛谢将那从以法莲来的军兵分别出来，叫他们回家去。故此，他们甚恼怒犹大人，气忿忿地回家去了。
verses.en: So Amaziah dismissed the troops that had come to him from Ephraim and sent them home.[NOTE:1] They were very angry at Judah and returned home incensed.
notes: Heb “and Amaziah separated them, the troops who came to him from Ephraim, to go to their place.”

verses.zh: 亚玛谢壮起胆来，率领他的民到盐谷，杀了西珥人一万。
verses.en: Amaziah boldly led his army to the Valley of Salt,[NOTE:1] where he defeated[NOTE:2] 10,000 Edomites.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and Amaziah strengthened himself and led his people and went to the Valley of Salt.”
Or “struck down.”
Heb “sons of Seir.”
verses.commentary:
25:11-13 These are shocking verses of death and brutality. Ancient warfare was honorable (esp. against Edom,
cf. 1 Kgs. 11:15).

25:11 "the Valley of Salt" This same location is mentioned in 2 Sam. 8:13; 1 Chr. 18:12. Its location is uncertain.

- east of Beersheba (wadi el-Ceba)

- south of the Dead Sea (wadi el-Milch)

verses.zh: 犹大人又生擒了一万带到山崖上，从那里把他们扔下去，以致他们都摔碎了。
verses.en: The men[NOTE:1] of Judah captured 10,000 men alive. They took them to the top of a cliff and threw them over.[NOTE:2] All the captives[NOTE:3] fell to their death.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “sons.”
Heb “and threw them from the top of the cliff.”
Heb “all of them.”
Heb “smashed in pieces.”

verses.zh: 但亚玛谢所打发回去、不许一同出征的那些军兵攻打犹大各城，从撒马利亚直到伯．和仑，杀了三千人，抢了许多财物。
verses.en: Now the troops Amaziah had dismissed and had not allowed to fight in the battle[NOTE:1] raided[NOTE:2] the cities of Judah from Samaria[NOTE:3] to Beth Horon. They killed[NOTE:4] 3,000 people and carried off a large amount of plunder.
notes: Heb “had sent back from going with him to the battle.”
Heb “stripped.”
For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.
Heb “struck down.”
verses.commentary:
25:13 "the troops" This refers to the mercenaries from Ephraim (2 Chr. 25:6). The phrase "the cities of Judah from
Samaria to Beth-horon" is unusual. Beth-horon is about fifteen miles NW of Jerusalem but "Samaria" is the capital of Israel,
much farther north; both are in Israel, not Judah.

This does explain v. 10 but the geography is uncertain. There is no "Samaria" near the border of Judah and
Ephraim. Perhaps this verse means they left from Samaria and traveled to Beth-horon, where they destroyed and plundered
villages while Amaziah was battling Edom.

verses.zh: 亚玛谢杀了以东人回来，就把西珥的神像带回，立为自己的神，在它面前叩拜烧香。
verses.en: When Amaziah returned from defeating the Edomites, he brought back the gods of the people[NOTE:1] of Seir and made them his personal gods.[NOTE:2] He bowed down before them and offered them sacrifices.
notes: Heb “sons.”
Heb “caused them to stand for him as gods.”
verses.commentary:
25:14 This is so shocking! How could a king who just responded positively to a prophet be led so quickly
into idolatry with the obviously impotent gods of Edom (cf. 15b)?

Notice what Amaziah did.

- collected the idols of Edom

- brought them to Jerusalem

- bowed down to them

- burned incense to them

1 Chronicles 25:15 is a powerfully logical statement! Why, Why, Why?

verses.zh: 因此，耶和华的怒气向亚玛谢发作，就差一个先知去见他，说：「这些神不能救它的民脱离你的手，你为何寻求它呢？」
verses.en: The Lord was angry at Amaziah and sent a prophet to him, who said, “Why are you following[NOTE:1] these gods[NOTE:2] that could not deliver their own people from your power?”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “seeking,” perhaps in the sense of “consulting [an oracle from].”
Heb “the gods of the people.”
Heb “hand.”
verses.commentary:
25:15 After the Davidic covenant of 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17 (i.e., 1 Kgs. 8:25), several ways of forgiveness
or restoration of fellowship with YHWH are mentioned.

- the possibility of repentance (i.e., 1 Kgs. 8:29-53)

- there is a prophetic warning (in this chapter alone there are two unnamed prophets and even a revelation from an idolatrous king)

verses.zh: 先知与王说话的时候，王对他说：「谁立你作王的谋士呢？你住口吧！为何找打呢？」先知就止住了，又说：「你行这事，不听从我的劝戒，我知道　神定意要灭你。」
verses.en: While he was speaking, Amaziah[NOTE:1] said to him, “Did we appoint you to be a royal counselor? Stop prophesying or else you will be killed!”[NOTE:2] So the prophet stopped, but added, “I know that God has decided[NOTE:3] to destroy you because you have done this thing and refused to listen to my advice.”
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Amaziah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “Stop yourself! Why should they strike you down?”

The verb יָעַץ (yaʿats, “has decided”) is from the same root as יוֹעֵץ (yoʿets, “counselor”) in v. 16 and עֵצָה (ʿetsah, “advice”) later in v. 16. The wordplay highlights the appropriate nature of the divine punishment. Amaziah rejected the counsel of God’s prophet; now he would be the victim of God’s “counsel.”
verses.commentary:
25:16 The king's rebellion is clearly revealed in this verse. His mind and heart were set on a course of idolatry!
But there will be consequences, as there always are!

verses.zh: 犹大王亚玛谢与群臣商议，就差遣使者去见耶户的孙子、约哈斯的儿子、以色列王约阿施，说：「你来，我们二人相见于战场。」
verses.en: After King Amaziah of Judah consulted with his advisers,[NOTE:1] he sent this message to the king of Israel, Joash son of Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu, “Come, face me on the battlefield.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “with his advisers” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “let us look at each other [in the] face.” The expression refers here not to a visit but to meeting in battle. See v. 21.
verses.commentary:
25:17 "took counsel" What counsel?

- he had rejected prophetic counsel, v. 16

- was this from

- his political leaders

- his military leaders

- his new gods and their priests

The counsel probably encouraged Amaziah to attack Israel because of what the Ephraimitic mercenaries did in v. 13.

verses.zh: 以色列王约阿施差遣使者去见犹大王亚玛谢，说：「黎巴嫩的蒺藜差遣使者去见黎巴嫩的香柏树，说：『将你的女儿给我儿子为妻。』后来黎巴嫩有一个野兽经过，把蒺藜践踏了。
verses.en: King Joash of Israel sent this message back to King Amaziah of Judah, “A thorn bush in Lebanon sent this message to a cedar in Lebanon, ‘Give your daughter to my son as a wife.’ Then a wild animal of Lebanon came by and trampled down the thorn bush.[NOTE:1]
notes: The thorn bush in the allegory is Judah. Amaziah’s success had deceived him into thinking he was on the same level as the major powers in the area (symbolized by the cedar). In reality he was not capable of withstanding an attack by a real military power such as Israel (symbolized by the wild animal).
verses.commentary:
25:18-19 Agricultural analogies or fables were common in the ANE (i.e., Samson). Judah thought she was a tree
but she was a bush!

What is surprising is Israel's humility and patience. YHWH was speaking through Israel's pagan king,
warning the Davidic seed. YHWH tries to sway human volition but He allows its choices and consequences. Life is not a
pre-written script. Foreknowledge must not be confused with determinism.

Apparently there was friendship between Judah and Israel.

- ability to hire mercenaries, 2 Chr. 25:6

- marriage proposal (i.e., even if rejected), 2 Chr. 25:18

- the king of Israel's attempt not to go to war, 2 Chr. 25:17-19

25:18 "the wild beast" This may be the 100,000 soldiers who were furious (cf. 2 Chr. 25:10).

verses.zh: 你说：『看哪，我打败了以东人』，你就心高气傲，以致矜夸。你在家里安居就罢了，为何要惹祸使自己和犹大国一同败亡呢？」
verses.en: You defeated Edom[NOTE:1] and it has gone to your head.[NOTE:2] Gloat over your success,[NOTE:3] but stay in your palace. Why bring calamity on yourself? Why bring down yourself and Judah along with you?”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “you say [to yourself], ‘look, you have defeated Edom.’”
Heb “and your heart is lifted up.”
Heb “to glorify.”
Heb “Why get involved in calamity and fall, you and Judah with you?”
verses.commentary:
25:19 King Amaziah was overconfident because of his defeat of a smaller Edomite army (i.e., 20,000 casualties),
but Israel was a much larger army.

verses.zh: 亚玛谢却不肯听从。这是出乎　神，好将他们交在敌人手里，因为他们寻求以东的神。
verses.en: But Amaziah did not heed the warning,[NOTE:1] for God wanted to hand them over to Joash because they followed the gods of Edom.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “did not listen.”
Heb “because it was from God in order to give them into the hand because they sought the gods of Edom.”
verses.commentary:
25:20 This is another theological comment by the Chronicler. YHWH is behind all history. Amaziah's idolatry will have
consequences, not only for him but for Judah.

verses.zh: 于是以色列王约阿施上来，在犹大的伯・示麦与犹大王亚玛谢相见于战场。
verses.en: So King Joash of Israel attacked. He and King Amaziah of Judah faced each other on the battlefield[NOTE:1] in Beth Shemesh of Judah.
notes: Heb “looked at each other [in the] face.” See the note on the expression “Come on, face me on the battlefield” in v. 17.
verses.commentary: 25:21 "Beth-shemesh" This (BDB 112) meant "house of the sun," which denoted astral worship in Judah at some point.

verses.zh: 犹大人败在以色列人面前，各自逃回家里去了。
verses.en: Judah was defeated by Israel, and each man ran back home.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and Judah was struck down before Israel and they fled, each to his tent.”

verses.zh: 以色列王约阿施在伯・示麦擒住约哈斯（就是亚哈谢）的孙子、约阿施的儿子、犹大王亚玛谢，将他带到耶路撒冷，又拆毁耶路撒冷的城墙，从以法莲门直到角门，共四百肘；
verses.en: King Joash of Israel captured King Amaziah of Judah, son of Joash son of Jehoahaz, in Beth Shemesh and brought him to Jerusalem. He broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate—a distance of about 600 feet.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “400 cubits.” Assuming a cubit of 18 inches (45 cm), the distance would have been about 600 feet (180 m).
verses.commentary:
25:23 Jerusalem's wall was the major means of her protection. Here, its destruction showed that YHWH's protection
had departed!

There are several items that show YHWH's judgment.

- a large portion (i.e., 600 feet) of the city's wall that faced north was destroyed

- the treasure and utensils of the temple were taken to Damascus

- members of the special temple Levites were taken (hostages, literally, "sons of pledges," cf. 2 Kgs. 14:14)

- the treasures of the king's palace were taken

- some time later his own servants conspired against him and slew him (same thing happened to Amaziah's father in
2 Chr. 24:25-26)

"cubits" See SPECIAL TOPIC: CUBIT.

verses.zh: 又将俄别・以东所看守　神殿里的一切金银和器皿，与王宫里的财宝都拿了去，并带人去为质，就回撒马利亚去了。
verses.en: He took away all the gold and silver, all the items found in God’s temple that were in the care of Obed-Edom, the riches in the royal palace, and some hostages. Then he went back to Samaria.

verses.zh: 以色列王约哈斯的儿子约阿施死后，犹大王约阿施的儿子亚玛谢又活了十五年。
verses.en: King Amaziah son of Joash of Judah lived for fifteen years after the death of King Joash son of Jehoahaz of Israel.

verses.zh: 亚玛谢其余的事，自始至终不都写在犹大和以色列诸王记上吗？
verses.en: The rest of the events of Amaziah’s reign, from start to finish, are recorded in the Scroll of the Kings of Judah and Israel.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “As for the rest of the events of Amaziah, the former and the latter, are they not—behold, they are written on the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel.”
verses.commentary:
25:26 "the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel" This book did not survive. In other places this book is mentioned as

- the Book of the Kings of Judah

- the Book of the Kings of Israel

but here, they are combined into one book. These records must be compilations of royal scribes through the
history of Israel and Judah. Therefore, they were finally combined sometime during the post-exilic period.

verses.zh: 自从亚玛谢离弃耶和华之后，在耶路撒冷有人背叛他，他就逃到拉吉；叛党却打发人到拉吉，将他杀了。
verses.en: From the time Amaziah turned from following the Lord, conspirators plotted against him in Jerusalem,[NOTE:1] so he fled to Lachish. But they sent assassins after him,[NOTE:2] and they killed him there.
notes: Heb “and they conspired against him [with] a conspiracy in Jerusalem.”
Heb “and they sent after him to Lachish.”
verses.commentary: 25:27 This is the second Judean king who was assassinated.

verses.zh: 人就用马将他的尸首驮回，葬在犹大京城他列祖的坟地里。
verses.en: His body was carried back by horses,[NOTE:1] and he was buried with his ancestors[NOTE:2] in the City of David.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and they carried him on horses.”
Heb “fathers.”

The phrase the City of David refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See 2 Sam 5:7.tc The Hebrew text has “Judah,” but some medieval mss read “David,” as does the parallel passage in 2 Kgs 14:20.
verses.commentary:
25:28 This implies that he was buried in the royal tombs. His reign, like so many of his predecessors' reigns, was a
mixture of faith and faithlessness!

"the city of Judah" Usually it says, "the city of David" (see LXX, Peshitta, Vulgate, cf. 2 Kgs. 14:20), which, in this
context, is Jerusalem, not Bethlehem.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why is 2 Chr. 25:1 a chronological problem?
